capabilities: Resolve {path} placeholders in a parent item's text from key:: value child bullets
Render the resolved summary inline in Live Preview, showing raw template on the cursor's line
Swap template and resolved values on fold and expand in Reading view
Look up values with dot-paths into nested lists up to 50 levels deep
Place templates at any level so any node summarizes its own subtree
disambiguation: Not a folding or outline-management tool; it computes and displays an inline rollup of a list item's own child bullets.
extras: Manual installation only (copy folder to .obsidian/plugins); ships a sample-test-note.md to verify behavior; the Live Preview feature uses editor internals and may not load on some builds, in which case Reading view still works; fold-tied behavior can vary by Obsidian version; not manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: Structured detail and a scannable overview pull in opposite directions: you either keep details visible and drown in them, or fold them away and lose the facts; the author wanted a computed view on the parent line without changing how notes are written.
problem: A folded bullet shows only its own text, so collapsed outlines lose the at-a-glance facts stored in their child items; Obsidian has no concept of per-list-item attributes or rollups.

relations.evidence: Outliner-first tools built around a node-with-attributes model — Logseq (block properties) and Tana
Logseq (block properties) and Tana (fields on nodes) — do "show a computed rollup on a node" natively

summary: Outline plugin that renders a template on a list item's line, pulling values from its nested child bullets so folded items read as summaries.
